61_breath_exhale_heart:
Breathe out longer. Your heart slows down.
Heart rate rises when you breathe in and falls when you breathe out: respiratory sinus arrhythmia (Hirsch & Bishop, 1981). A longer exhale gives the brake more time.
Try it: in for 4, out for 8.
Did your heart slow down?

62_cold_shock_first_30s:
Can't breathe in the ice bath? That's not weakness.
Cold shock: in the first 30 seconds you gasp, breathing races and heart rate jumps. In one study, 5 short immersions clearly reduced that response (Tipton et al., 1998).
Short. Controlled. Never alone.
How did your first one feel?

63_grip_vs_blood_pressure:
Your doctor checks your blood pressure. Nobody checks your grip.
In ~140,000 adults in 17 countries, every 5 kg less grip strength was linked to 16% higher risk of death, and grip predicted cardiovascular death better than systolic blood pressure (Leong et al., 2015). An association, not proof.
When did you last test your grip?

64_fit_vs_fat:
You lost the weight. Are you safe now?
In a meta-analysis, unfit people had about twice the risk of death regardless of BMI, while overweight-but-fit people had a similar risk to normal-weight-fit people (Barry et al., 2014).
The scale tells you one thing. Fitness tells you more.
Weight or fitness: what do you track?

65_muscle_loss_per_decade:
You're losing muscle. Right now. Quietly.
After 30, adults lose about 3–8% of muscle mass per decade, faster after 60 (Volpi et al., 2004). The scale won't show it.
Strength training fights it back. Measure, then build.
When did you last measure your muscle mass?
